question: If $A = \begin{bmatrix}1&0&2\\0&2&1\\2&0&3\end{bmatrix}$, then show that $A^3 - 6A^2 + 7A + 2I = O$.
explanation:
**Step 1:** Compute the matrix squared $A^2$ by performing row-by-column matrix multiplication of $A$ with itself: $A^2 = \begin{bmatrix}1&0&2\\0&2&1\\2&0&3\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0&2\\0&2&1\\2&0&3\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}1+0+4&0+0+0&2+0+6\\0+0+2&0+4+0&0+2+3\\2+0+6&0+0+0&4+0+9\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}5&0&8\\2&4&5\\8&0&13\end{bmatrix}$.
**Step 2:** Compute the matrix cubed $A^3$ by multiplying $A^2$ by $A$: $A^3 = \begin{bmatrix}5&0&8\\2&4&5\\8&0&13\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}1&0&2\\0&2&1\\2&0&3\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}5+0+16&0+0+0&10+0+24\\2+0+10&0+8+0&4+4+15\\8+0+26&0+0+0&16+0+39\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}21&0&34\\12&8&23\\34&0&55\end{bmatrix}$.
**Step 3:** Substitute the derived matrices $A^3$ and $A^2$, along with matrix $A$ and the identity matrix $I$, into the left-hand side of the expression: $LHS = \begin{bmatrix}21&0&34\\12&8&23\\34&0&55\end{bmatrix} - 6\begin{bmatrix}5&0&8\\2&4&5\\8&0&13\end{bmatrix} + 7\begin{bmatrix}1&0&2\\0&2&1\\2&0&3\end{bmatrix} + 2\begin{bmatrix}1&0&0\\0&1&0\\0&0&1\end{bmatrix}$.
**Step 4:** Simplify by scaling each matrix and performing element-wise matrix addition and subtraction: $LHS = \begin{bmatrix}21&0&34\\12&8&23\\34&0&55\end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix}30&0&48\\12&24&30\\48&0&78\end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix}7&0&14\\0&14&7\\14&0&21\end{bmatrix} + \begin{bmatrix}2&0&0\\0&2&0\\0&0&2\end{bmatrix}$. Combining corresponding elements results in a matrix where every entry is exactly $0$, which matches the zero matrix $O$. Hence proved.
